title: incident chronicle: compact timeline aggregator and contextual action hints for faster triage
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds an on-call facing compact incident timeline and a lightweight action-suggester that surfaces prioritized next steps. No API/consumer-facing changes. Enable behind feature flag 'incident_chronicle_v1' by default off for 2 weeks rollout.
description:
Summary: This PR adds 'Incident Chronicle'—a compact timeline aggregator that synthesizes recent traces, alerts, deploys, config-changes, and log highlights into a single chronological digest, plus a lightweight contextual action-hints engine that suggests prioritized next steps and an abbreviated runbook fragment.
Motivation: oncall handoffs and first-minute triage are often slowed by hunting through multiple dashboards. The Chronicle reduces cognitive load by showing a concise, scored narrative and actionable hints (restart, config revert, roll forward, run-sanity-checks) derived from heuristics and quick telemetry checks.
Checklist:
- implement timeline aggregator and scoring heuristics
- add action-hints engine and rule-set editor
- UI: compact drawer in incident-bot slack/CLI output
- add feature-flag and rollout gating
- instrument metrics and add smoke tests
- update docs and playbook examples
What changed (high-level):
- core: services/chronicle/* adds timeline builder, event normalizer, scorer and action-hints engine
- integrations: connectors for traces (observability-pack), deploy metadata (k8s events), recent alerts indices
- api: incident-bot/handlers/chronicle_handler.go exposes /v1/incident-chronicle (internal)
- cli: incident-bot/cli/brief command with --chronicle flag that returns compact digest
- ui: slack blocks payload generator and compact runbook fragment
- tests: unit + e2e smoke tests and a small synthetic incident fixture
Commits (summary):
- 6 commits total: initial aggregator prototype; add normalizer and event timestamps; integrate deploy metadata; build scoring rules and test harness; add CLI and Slack payloads; docs & feature-flag gating.
Changed files (representative):
- services/chronicle/aggregator.go
- services/chronicle/scorer.go
- services/chronicle/rules.json
- incident-bot/handlers/chronicle_handler.go
- incident-bot/cli/brief.go
- integrations/k8s/deploy_events.go
- integrations/traces/trace_indexer.go
- tests/fixtures/chronic_incident.json
- docs/oncall/chronicle.md
- web/slack/chronicle_blocks.go
Edge cases & safeguards:
- Feature-flagged rollout with opt-in for teams; scoring uses conservative thresholds to avoid noisy false positives; action hints include safety links and exact runbook fragment only for fully matched rules; any hint that would trigger automated remediation is explicit and requires additional confirmation.
Observability & SLOs: added metrics incident_chronicle.generated, incident_chronicle.hints_emitted, and latency histogram; alerting on error rate >1% for 5m.
Backwards compat: internal API only; no external contract changes.
Testing & CI: initial CI run failed on lint for a slack block helper; fixed formatting and re-ran, CI passed.
Review timeline and convo:
- Samir: "Nice compact output; can we make scoring weights configurable per-team and persist defaults?"
- Priya: "Agree—added a rules.json and a simple editor in the handler for team defaults; storing defaults is gated behind team opt-in."
- Olivia: "Concern: risk of action-hints recommending restarts too aggressively during canary deploys."
- Priya: "Adjusted rule to use deploy window and success-rate heuristics before suggesting restart; added test fixture."
- Diego: "Docs look good; please add an example for paging process owners in Slack block."
- Priya: "Added Slack mention template and test."
Approvals: Samir and Olivia approved after follow-ups.
Merging: squash-merged to main after green CI and a brief canary run in staging for 24h.
Rollout plan: enable feature flag for internal SRE team (canary) for 48h, then expand to 25% org usage, monitor hints_emitted and false-positive feedback metric, fully enable after 2 weeks if stable.
Related: builds on ideas from ENG-1843 (fast-triage heuristics) and PRs that add compact snapshots.
Notes for oncall: added docs/oncall/chronicle.md with sample outputs and suggested triage flow.
